title: The explicit pro-etale tensor pullback comparison preserves composite adjunction units
statement:
Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be morphisms of schemes, with the small pro-etale sites, base-change functors $B_f$ and inverse images of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use compatible small skeletons as in that definition. Let $R_V,R_W,R_Z$ be sheaves of commutative rings on the respective sites and fix ring-sheaf isomorphisms $c_k:k^{-1}R_V\xrightarrow{\sim}R_W$ and $c_h:h^{-1}R_W\xrightarrow{\sim}R_Z$. Let $a_{h,k}:h^{-1}k^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(k\circ h)^{-1}$ be the inverse-image composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition], transported along the canonical fibre-product isomorphisms $q_U:B_hB_kU\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{k\circ h}U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use its induced comparison on ring sheaves, and set $c_{k\circ h}=c_h\circ h^{-1}(c_k)\circ(a_{h,k,R_V})^{-1}$.

Write $f^*M=f^{-1}M\otimes_{f^{-1}R_{\mathrm{target}},c_f}R_{\mathrm{source}}$ for the module pullbacks of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Form the explicit tensor comparison $t_{h,k}:h^*k^*\to(k\circ h)^*$ by applying $a_{h,k}$ to the inverse-image factor and multiplying the intermediate scalar into the final scalar. More precisely, on local tensor generators, after the canonical inverse-image and tensor identifications (inverse image commutes with $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ and with colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], hence with relative tensor products, which are coequalizers of $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$), it sends $(m\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $m\otimes c_h(a)b$; here $m$ is a local section of $h^{-1}k^{-1}M$, $a$ a local section of $h^{-1}R_W$, and $b$ a local section of $R_Z$. Its inverse sends $m\otimes b$ to $(m\otimes1)\otimes b$, using $a_{h,k}^{-1}$ on $m$.

Then these local formulas give mutually inverse natural module-sheaf maps, and this explicit comparison is compatible with the specified adjunctions, not just an unspecified isomorphism of their underlying functors. Precisely, let $d_{h,k}:(k\circ h)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}k_*h_*$ be restriction along $q_U$ on sections (with the module actions induced by the specified coefficient maps), and let $\eta^f$ be the unit of $f^*\dashv f_*$. For every $R_V$-module sheaf $M$,
$$
 k_*h_*(t_{h,k,M})\circ k_*(\eta^h_{k^*M})\circ\eta^k_M
 =d_{h,k,(k\circ h)^*M}\circ\eta^{k\circ h}_M.
$$
Thus $t_{h,k}$ is the unique left-adjoint comparison corresponding to $d_{h,k}$ under [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] and the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction].

proof.text: For every object $U$ of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the universal property of fibre products gives $q_U:Z\times_W(W\times_VU)\cong Z\times_VU$: its components are the projection to $Z$ and the composite projection to $U$. The inverse has components the projection to $Z$ and the pair of projections to $W,U$. Both composites have the original projections, hence are identities by uniqueness. The same uniqueness proves naturality in $U$. The inverse-image definition supplies covering-preserving, finite-limit-preserving site functors, so the site-composition lemma applies. Transporting its comparison along $q$ yields $a_{h,k}$ and the right comparison $d^0$ on underlying sheaves. Write $j^f_F:F\to f_*f^{-1}F$ for the sheaf unit. The cited unit compatibility says, sectionwise, $a_{h,k,F}(j^h_{k^{-1}F}(j^k_F(m)))=d^0_{(kh)^{-1}F}(j^{kh}_F(m))$, with the left side evaluated on $B_hB_kU$ and $m\in F(U)$. This is the underlying sheaf-unit identity used below.

Put $A=h^{-1}k^{-1}R_V$, $B=h^{-1}R_W$, $C=R_Z$, $N=h^{-1}k^{-1}M$, $\alpha=h^{-1}c_k$ and $\beta=c_h$. The tensor and colimit assertions of the inverse-image lemma identify $h^*k^*M$ with $(N\otimes_{A,\alpha}B)\otimes_{B,\beta}C$. Indeed, the relative tensor is the coequalizer of the two action maps on $F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G$, and both tensor factors and this coequalizer are preserved. The same lemma says that $a_{h,k}$ is monoidal, so, using $c_{kh}a_{h,k,R_V}=\beta\alpha$, the target identifies with $N\otimes_{A,\beta\alpha}C$. Define $T((m\otimes a)\otimes b)=m\otimes\beta(a)b$. For $r\in A$, the relation $(rm\otimes a)=(m\otimes\alpha(r)a)$ is preserved because $rm\otimes\beta(a)b=m\otimes\beta\alpha(r)\beta(a)b$. The outer $B$-balancing is preserved by multiplicativity of $\beta$. Conversely $S(m\otimes b)=(m\otimes1)\otimes b$ is $A$-balanced since $(rm\otimes1)\otimes b=(m\otimes\alpha(r))\otimes b=(m\otimes1)\otimes\beta\alpha(r)b$. Thus $TS=1$, and $ST=1$ by the outer balancing relation. The formulas are additive and $C$-linear, and commute with restriction maps and morphisms in $M$. By the definition of sheaf tensor product as sheafification of the sectionwise tensor, these maps give inverse natural sheaf maps; reinsert $a_{h,k}$ in $T$ and its inverse in $S$. This is exactly $t_{h,k}$.

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules, together with Tag 03EL tensor-product-pullback

proof.text: For a coefficient ring sheaf write $\rho_f=f_*c_f\circ j^f_{R_{\mathrm{target}}}$. The module-operation definition makes $f_*$ act through $\rho_f$, and its module unit sends $m$ to $j^f_M(m)\otimes1$: under its stated identification $f^*M\cong f^{-1}M$ by $x\otimes r\mapsto c_f^{-1}(r)x$, this is exactly $j^f_M$. Apply the sheaf-unit identity of Step 1 to $R_V$. Naturality with respect to $c_k$, followed by $c_h$ and the equality $c_{kh}a_{h,k,R_V}=c_hh^{-1}c_k$, gives $d^0_{R_Z}\rho_{kh}=k_*\rho_h\circ\rho_k$. Hence restriction along $q_U$ respects the $R_V$-actions on $(kh)_*P$ and $k_*h_*P$ for every $R_Z$-module $P$; restriction along $q_U^{-1}$ gives its inverse. This is the specified natural module isomorphism $d_{h,k}$. Finally the composite-adjunction definition gives its left adjoint $h^*k^*$ the unit $k_*(\eta^h_{k^*M})\circ\eta^k_M$.

Evaluate both sides of the claimed unit equation at $U\in V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $m\in M(U)$. By Step 3 the successive units send $m$ first to $j^k_M(m)\otimes1$, then to $(w\otimes1)\otimes1$, where $w=j^h_{k^{-1}M}(j^k_M(m))$ on $B_hB_kU$. Step 2 sends this to $a_{h,k,M}(w)\otimes1$, since $c_h(1)=1$. The right side sends $m$ to the restriction along $q_U$ of $j^{kh}_M(m)\otimes1$. Naturality of the tensor restriction maps makes this $d^0_{(kh)^{-1}M}(j^{kh}_M(m))\otimes1$, equal to the left side by Step 1. This checks every section of $M$, hence proves the equality of sheaf maps and therefore the displayed natural-transformation equality. Apply the conjugate-iso/unit-equation lemma with $L_1=h^*k^*$, $R_1=k_*h_*$, $L_2=(kh)^*$, $R_2=(kh)_*$ and $\delta=d_{h,k}$. The unit of the first adjunction is exactly the composite unit just calculated, so the lemma proves the asserted uniqueness of this explicit comparison.
